tables.purpose: Tracks each marketing campaign with its details and outcomes.

column_meanings.meaning: Unique identifier for a marketing campaign.
Descriptive name given to the campaign.
Marketing channel used for the campaign (e.g., social_media, affiliate, paid_search).
Date the campaign began or is scheduled to begin.
Date the campaign ended or is scheduled to end; may be null for ongoing campaigns.
Monetary budget allocated to the campaign.
Current lifecycle status of the campaign (e.g., active, completed, paused).

tables.business_value: Enables analysis of campaign performance, budgeting, and channel effectiveness across time.

ambiguity_flags.note: The column name 'channel' also appears in the orders table with different observed values (in_store, marketplace, mobile_app). No foreign key links; meaning is ambiguous across tables.
The column name 'status' appears in customers, orders, and products tables with differing value sets and no foreign key relationship, so its specific meaning is ambiguous.

tables.purpose: Stores basic profile information for each customer.

column_meanings.meaning: Unique identifier for a customer.
Customer's email address, used as a contact identifier.
Customer's given name.
Customer's family name.
Date the customer account was created.
Country associated with the customer.
Marketing segment classification (e.g., new, at_risk, regular, high_value).
Current account status (e.g., active, inactive, churned).

tables.business_value: Provides a basis for segmentation, targeting, and lifecycle management of the customer base.

ambiguity_flags.note: The column name 'status' also appears in marketing_campaigns, orders, and products tables with different value sets and no foreign key relationship, making its precise meaning ambiguous across tables.

tables.purpose: Records each purchase transaction made by customers.

column_meanings.meaning: Unique identifier for an order.
Reference to the customer who placed the order.
Timestamp when the order was created.
Current state of the order (e.g., cancelled, refunded).
Sales channel through which the order was placed (e.g., in_store, marketplace, mobile_app).
Total monetary value of the order.

tables.business_value: Allows tracking of sales volume, channel performance, and order fulfillment outcomes.

ambiguity_flags.note: The column name 'status' also exists in marketing_campaigns, customers, and products tables with differing values and no foreign key relationship; its meaning is ambiguous across tables.
The column name 'channel' also appears in marketing_campaigns with different observed values (social_media, affiliate, paid_search). No foreign key links; meaning is ambiguous across tables.

tables.purpose: Details the individual products included in each order.

column_meanings.meaning: Unique identifier for an order line item.
Reference to the order that contains this item.
Reference to the product being purchased.
Number of units of the product in this line item.
Price per unit of the product at the time of the order.

tables.relationships: order_id references orders.order_id; product_id references products.product_id
tables.business_value: Enables analysis of product-level sales, average order value, and inventory demand.

tables.purpose: Catalogues items that can be sold.

column_meanings.meaning: Unique identifier for a product.
Descriptive name of the product.
Category or group the product belongs to.
Standard selling price of the product.
Current availability status (e.g., active, discontinued, out_of_stock).

tables.business_value: Supports product inventory management, pricing strategy, and category performance reporting.

ambiguity_flags.note: The column name 'status' also appears in marketing_campaigns, customers, and orders tables with different value sets and no foreign key relationship, so its precise meaning is ambiguous across tables.
